newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-DANES CRUSH AMERICANS IN U.S. CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DANES CRUSH AMERICANS IN U.S. CUP.

text.p: Danish striker Per Pedersen, born in Hans-Christian Andersen's hometown of Odense, lived out a real-life fairy tale Wednesday by scoring four goals including a first-half hat trick as Denmark outclassed the United States 4-1 in a U.S. Cup match.

The ugly-duckling image of the Danes was transformed into a beautiful swan of flowing football on a wet night in the Rose Bowl, leaving the American defenders wandering around like Hansel and Gretel lost in the woods.
Pedersen, who plays for his hometown club Odense Boldklub in the Danish league, had scored only once before for his country in five internationals.
For the Americans, who face crucial World Cup regional qualifying matches starting in two months, the third loss in three U.S. Cup matches was a bitter disappointment.

Coach Steve Sampson was forced to experiment with several young internationally inexperienced players in place of such regulars as captain John Harkes and leading goalscorer Eric Wynalda both recovering from injury.

Pedersen, 27, struck in the 16th minute when defender Alexi Lalas weakly headed out. The Danish striker chested the ball down, beat Jeff Agoos and drilled a low left-footer past goalkeeper Brad Friedel.

Ten minutes later he scored with a similar low angled shot and completed his hat-trick on the stroke of half-time with an almost identical left-foot blast, seconds after Joe-Max Moore had pulled one back for the Americans with a curling free-kick over the defensive wall.
Just ten minutes into the second half, Pedersen was mobbed by teammates when he hooked home a loose ball for his fourth goal. He was substituted five minutes from the end.

Denmark, the 1992 European champions, were playing without British-based star players such as goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel and striker Brian Laudrup. They had lost the first match of the four-nation tournament 3-1 but rallied to beat Peru on Sunday 2-1.
But Wednesday's emphatic victory was not enough to win the U.S. Cup title. Mexico, who also beat the United States 2-1 on Sunday, was playing Peru later in the evening for the championship.

United States - Brad Friedel (Mark Dodd, 46th minute), Dan Calichman. Mike Burns, Jeff Agoos, Alexi Lalas, Steve Ralston (Jason Kreis, 57th), Cobi Jones, Claudio Reyna, Roy Lassiter (Brian McBride, 33rd), Jovan Kirovski (Preki Radosavljevic 63rd), Joe-Max Moore

Denmark - Mogens Krogh, Soren Colding, Michael Hemmingsen, Per Nielsen, Brian Steen Nielsen, Soren Andersen, Per Pedersen (Peter Moller, 85th), Steen Nedergaard, Jens Jessen, Ulrik Pedersen (Stig Tofting, 72nd), Jesper Thygesen
